test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What type of majority is required to pass laws under Articles 2 and 3, as per Article 4(2) in Indian parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Simple majority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Articles 2 and 3** of the Indian Constitution deal with the admission or establishment of new states and the alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• As per **Article 4(2)**, laws made under Articles 2 and 3 require only a **simple majority** in Parliament, not a special or two-thirds majority.
 
• A **simple majority** means that the majority of members present and voting in each house of Parliament is sufficient to pass the law.
 
• Unlike constitutional amendments (which often require special or two-thirds majorities), these laws are considered ordinary legislation.
 
• This provision ensures flexibility in reorganizing states to address administrative and political needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Majority:**

 
 
• A simple majority is achieved when more than 50% of the members present and voting support a motion.
 
• This is the most commonly used voting method for passing ordinary bills in Parliament.
 
• It excludes abstentions and absent members from the total count.
 
 
 
• **Special Majority:**
 
 
• A special majority requires a higher threshold, such as two-thirds of the members present and voting, or in some cases, two-thirds of the total membership of the house.
 
• It is typically required for constitutional amendment bills under Article 368.
 
 
 
• **State Reorganization:**
 
 
• State reorganization involves altering the boundaries, names, or areas of states to address linguistic, cultural, or administrative concerns.
 
• Examples include the formation of Telangana in 2014 and the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Articles 2 and 3:**
 
 
• Article 2 allows Parliament to admit new states or establish new states on terms it deems fit.
 
• Article 3 enables the reorganization of states through changes in boundaries, areas, and names.
 
 
 
• **Article 4(2):**
 
 
• It specifies that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not considered constitutional amendments.
 
• Thus, they can be enacted through a simple majority, unlike constitutional amendment bills.
